title: 2BHK flat, Bengaluru (BBMP area), 11-month agreement
model: stub built from backend tools (agent loop pending)
agreement_text:
C1. Monthly rent is INR 25000 and the refundable security deposit is INR 150000.
C2. The entire deposit is forfeited on any breach or early exit.
C3. Six lock-in months remain, payable at the monthly rent on early exit.
C4. A fixed painting charge of INR 15000 is deducted on exit.
C5. Annual rent escalation is 15 percent.
C6. Two months' notice is required; one month has been given.

governing_law.summary: The Karnataka Rent Act, 1999 does not apply to this flat: it was built in 2019, inside the 15-year exemption in s.2(3)(f). The Part A rent ceiling in s.2(3)(e) turns on the statutory standard rent, not the Rs 25,000 market rent, so it is not relied on. The lease is governed by the agreement itself, read with the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 and the Indian Contract Act, 1872.

reasons.text: Obtain deemed/standard rent; monthly market rent alone does not establish this exclusion.
The stated construction/substantial-renovation age is below the section 2(3)(f) fifteen-year period.

findings.clause_text: The entire deposit is forfeited on any breach or early exit.
findings.issue: The whole deposit is forfeited on any breach or early exit, whatever the landlord's actual loss. Excessive forfeiture is a penalty; only reasonable compensation is recoverable.
findings.ask: Replace forfeiture with deduction of actual, itemised loss.

findings.clause_text: Six lock-in months remain, payable at the monthly rent on early exit.
findings.issue: Leaving early costs the rent for all six remaining lock-in months, on top of the deposit forfeiture in C2.
findings.ask: Cap the early-exit payment at one month's rent, or waive it if a replacement tenant is found.

findings.clause_text: A fixed painting charge of INR 15000 is deducted on exit.
findings.issue: A fixed painting charge applies even if the walls are in the condition received. Restoration excludes reasonable wear and tear.
findings.ask: Charge painting only for damage beyond reasonable wear and tear, judged against the dated move-in checklist.

findings.issue: A 15% yearly increase is above Dhara's 10% fairness threshold.
findings.ask: Revise the increase to 10% a year.
findings.money_note: (15 - 10)% of Rs 3,00,000 annual rent. The 10% is a product threshold, not a legal limit.

findings.clause_text: Two months' notice is required; one month has been given.
findings.issue: Two months' notice is required and one has been given, so one month's rent is exposed.
findings.ask: Agree that the notice already given counts, or reduce the notice period to one month.
